ranked.headline: Deep learning aligns, segments and spatially resolves cells across microscopy and omics
ranked.summary: Self-supervised and multimodal models are now applied to registration, segmentation and spatial transcriptomics across histology, CODEX, TEM and cryo-ET.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein language model embeddings drive task-specific prediction models
ranked.summary: November 2025 papers pair protein language model embeddings with structure, retrieval and task-specific networks for function and interaction prediction.

ranked.headline: Statistical and graph-based inference of regulatory structure from single-cell data
ranked.summary: Single-cell resolution now supports testing expression along pseudotime and cell-state-resolved genetic association, not only discrete cell-type calls.

ranked.headline: Learned fusion of histology, cfDNA and omics data for cancer subtyping and prediction
ranked.summary: Recent items pair learned models with histology, cfDNA and spatial profiles to infer mutations, subtypes and immunotherapy response.

ranked.headline: Latent models disentangle cell-cycle, batch and perturbation effects in single-cell data
ranked.summary: Explicit latent partitioning and reference-based mapping now target confounded single-cell and multi-omics measurements directly.

ranked.headline: Graph-based networks couple feature interactions with incomplete multi-omics integration
ranked.summary: Published November 2025 work pairs feature-interaction graphs with missing-omics recovery to support integrative multi-omics analysis.

ranked.headline: Graph neural networks predict biological interactions from multimodal and network data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair graph neural networks with pretrained embeddings to predict drug, protein, gene, and microbial associations.

ranked.headline: Topology and multimodal learning prioritize drug repurposing and synergy candidates
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply network topology, explainable learning and uncertainty-aware models to repurposing and drug synergy prediction.

ranked.headline: Neural models infer biological features directly from raw nanopore and genomic data
ranked.summary: Deep models are now trained on raw nanopore traces and single-cell atlases, shifting learning-based inference closer to primary sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and new callers assess variant detection across reads and reference genomes
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and new callers examine how sequencing technology, reference choice, and method design shape variant sensitivity and concordance.

ranked.headline: Learned DNA sequence models predict methylation, TF binding and enhancer interactions
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend sequence-based regulatory models to personalized diploid genomes, Hi-C chromatin structure, and synthetic-data fine-tuning.

ranked.headline: Spatial transcriptomics models cell-state trajectories across developmental time points
ranked.summary: Sequential spatial slides and multi-timepoint optimal transport now allow trajectory inference that jointly models tissue position and temporal ordering.

ranked.headline: Packaged, reproducible pipelines span raw reads to taxonomic and functional inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and published tools package QC, assembly, annotation, and probe design into reproducible software, with some now browser-based or real-time.

ranked.headline: Generative models extend biomolecular structure prediction toward conformational ensembles
ranked.summary: Benchmarks and SE(3)-equivariant trajectory generators now test whether learned models capture protein conformational dynamics beyond single structures.

ranked.headline: Generative models for molecular design face harder, benchmark-driven evaluation
ranked.summary: MolGenBench tests structure-based generators across 120 protein targets and 220,005 confirmed actives in a hit-to-lead setting.

ranked.headline: Interpretable models link microbial sequence features to interaction and resistance
ranked.summary: Models that expose which sequence features or microbial variables drive predictions are now applied across phage, resistance, and microbiome tasks.

ranked.headline: Inferring cell type-specific regulation from perturbation, reporter and multi-omic data
ranked.summary: Perturbation, reporter, and population-scale datasets now resolve regulatory activity to individual cell types, tissues, and designed sequence elements.

ranked.headline: Structure- and sequence-based prediction of protein binding and its evaluation
ranked.summary: Integrated sequence-structure models and independent benchmarks now test binding affinity, complex geometry and mutational ΔΔG predictions against other tools.

ranked.headline: Parameter inference and surrogate modeling extend biological models fit to data
ranked.summary: Single-cell and ODE-based fitting tools now infer kinetic and interaction parameters directly from high-dimensional biological measurements.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking metagenomic abundance, binning and functional recovery
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications address database curation, sequencing depth limits, and consensus differential abundance testing in microbiome data.

ranked.headline: Automated tools link public biomedical data sources into queryable biological networks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications describe tools that mine literature, transcriptomic and identifier resources into analysable network representations.

ranked.headline: Purpose-built R and Python tools target single bottlenecks in omics analysis workflows
ranked.summary: Recent publications and preprints add reproducible, narrowly scoped tools for amplicon, single-cell, metabolomics and holo-omics data analysis.

ranked.headline: Computational tools extract epigenetic and expression features from sequencing data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints benchmark nanopore basecalling for m6A and model cfDNA fragmentation to infer gene expression and regulatory activity.

ranked.headline: Association methods increasingly account for relatedness and locus or gene specificity
ranked.summary: Relatedness-aware effect estimation and specificity-based gene prioritization are being validated on UK Biobank and EHR phenotype data.

ranked.headline: Redesigned algorithms cut memory and runtime across alignment, motif, and read analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications target memory and runtime bottlenecks in alignment, motif scoring, genome size estimation, and DNA storage read processing.

ranked.headline: Computational tools assign viral genomes to hosts and taxa at scale
ranked.summary: Host and taxonomic annotation of viral genomes is scaling, while a 27-tool benchmark shows accuracy is context-dependent.

ranked.headline: Open software for crystal detection, ligand kinetics, breeding, and metabolic modeling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers release physics-based, machine learning, and simulation methods as runnable software for direct lab use.

ranked.headline: Long-read and population methylomes reveal context-dependent DNA methylation diversity
ranked.summary: Long-read and population-scale methods now resolve methylation diversity and genome variation across Arabidopsis, human populations, and organelle genomes.

ranked.headline: Automating cofolding-to-MD preparation and learned models for protein dynamics
ranked.summary: Learned analysis and automated system preparation are being chained into pipelines that link structure prediction to molecular dynamics.

ranked.headline: Interpretable models linking genetic markers to phenotypes, variants and risk
ranked.summary: Sparse priors, calibration analyses, and latent multimodal encodings now extend genetic prediction beyond scalar association outputs.

ranked.headline: Generative, docking, and QSAR models drive prospective ligand design and screening
ranked.summary: Prospective experimental validation of AI-guided generative, docking, and QSAR designs now appears alongside covalent-docking tool reviews.

ranked.headline: Population-scale mapping of plasmids, transposons and phages across bacterial genomes
ranked.summary: Large clinical genome collections and benchmarked short-read plasmid tools make mobile element exchange measurable across bacterial populations.

ranked.headline: Structure-aware and spectrum-level computational handling of peptide modifications in MS
ranked.summary: Deep learning and spectrum-level methods now resolve peptide modifications across retention, fragmentation, and PTM isoform assignment in MS proteomics.

ranked.headline: Simulations tie resistance, transport, and resource supply to microbial outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent simulation studies treat resistance development, time-varying transport, and resource structure as tunable variables within explicit dynamical models.

ranked.headline: MD and network analyses map allosteric pathways linking RNA dynamics to protein binding
ranked.summary: Recent MD and network studies resolve how single sequence changes and binding partners reshape RNA and RNA recognition motif allosteric communication.

ranked.headline: Pretrained nucleotide and gene language models drive genome annotation tasks
ranked.summary: Recent work extends sequence foundation models to plant genome annotation, mRNA, metagenomic genes and transposable element classification.

ranked.headline: Computational methods for validating and building biomolecular structure models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published tool pair machine-learned potentials, blind CASP16 benchmarking, and RNA ensemble ranking to test structural models.

ranked.headline: Consistent phylogenetic inference under ILS and networks, with genome-scale confidence
ranked.summary: Scalable methods now pair statistical consistency with explicit confidence quantification, including a two-million-genome SARS-CoV-2 tree.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale assemblies and genomic resources across annelid, cricket and tunicate
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend chromosome-level assembly, annotation and comparative resources to annelid, cricket, tunicate and scallop taxa.

ranked.headline: Machine learning and flux models infer enzyme and metabolic capabilities across microbes
ranked.summary: Genome-scale strain models and mining of over 10,000 fermented-food genomes extend enzyme and metabolic prediction beyond individual organisms.
